kept.excerpt: Claude Fable 5 has been re-deployed and is now available globally for all users. We’re taking this opportunity to share further information in two areas. First, we provide more information on the cybersecurity safeguards—specifically, the safety classifiers—that we launched with the model.
kept.relevance: This recent official status update documents public availability and the role of safeguards for a frontier model whose Fable name does not qualify under the Opus-specific resolution rules.

kept.excerpt: On Friday, June 12, the US government applied export controls to our newest models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. Because the order took effect immediately and we had no reliable way to verify nationality in real-time, we suspended access to both models for all users. As of today, June 30, the export controls on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 have been lifted. Fable 5 will be available starting tomorrow, Wednesday, July 1, to users globally on the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.
kept.relevance: The suspension and restoration establish a contemporaneous example of regulatory and safeguard issues affecting actual public model availability, which is essential to qualification.

kept.excerpt: Claude Sonnet 5 is built to be the most agentic Sonnet model yet. Sonnet 5 narrows the gap: its performance is close to that of Opus 4.8, but at lower prices. From today, Claude Sonnet 5 is available across all plans: it is the default model for Free and Pro plans, and is available to Max, Team, and Enterprise users.
kept.relevance: This late-June announcement provides a dated reference to Opus 4.8 in the active lineup and shows continued model releases under a name that does not itself qualify.

kept.excerpt: We’re upgrading Claude Opus to a new version: Claude Opus 4.8. It builds on Opus 4.7 with improvements across benchmarks, and is a more effective collaborator. It’s available today for the same price.
kept.relevance: This establishes the latest dated Opus launch found before the experiment cutoff and supplies the most recent observation for evaluating Opus release cadence.

kept.excerpt: Our latest model, Claude Opus 4.7, is now generally available. Opus 4.7 is available today across all Claude products and our API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Pricing remains the same as Opus 4.6: $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.
kept.relevance: This official public launch supplies a prior Opus release date and illustrates the explicit availability language that would satisfy the resolution standard for a successor.

kept.excerpt: The new Claude Opus 4.6 improves on its predecessor’s coding skills. Claude Opus 4.6 is available today on claude.ai, our API, and all major cloud platforms. If you’re a developer, use `claude-opus-4-6` via the Claude API.
kept.relevance: This earlier 2026 Opus launch adds a historical cadence observation and confirms that public API access accompanied the announcement.

kept.excerpt: Our newest model, Claude Opus 4.5, is available today. Opus 4.5 is available today on our apps, our API, and on all three major cloud platforms. If you’re a developer, simply use `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` via the Claude API.
kept.relevance: This provides an additional recent historical Opus release date for assessing the distribution of intervals between publicly accessible Opus versions.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-10, inclusive. Selected seven dated official Anthropic announcements covering recent status, public-access constraints, naming distinctions, and historical Opus launches. Excluded prediction-market pages, unknown-date material, post-cutoff publications, and later edits; in particular, omitted later pricing edits to the Sonnet announcement. Publication dates were verified in web_search results containing the dated source text. web_fetch failed because of a provider-configuration error; the agent-reach skill's web-read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so no further fallback attempts were made. Excerpts therefore rely on indexed source text rather than independently retrieved archival snapshots. No selected source establishes a committed public release date for the next Opus model.
